themes_detail.label: Curb Deterioration Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Curb condition complaints spiked to 16 THIS WEEK, a 456% increase versus the 2.9-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks, suggesting a sudden infrastructure failure affecting sidewalk access and pedestrian safety across the district.
evidence: 16 curb condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.9 weekly average (z-score: 9.63)
456% increase represents the most statistically extreme spike in the dataset
Aligns with broader street condition complaints (968 total over 90 days), suggesting systemic deterioration
reporting_angles: Canvass affected blocks to document specific curb damage; photograph locations and assess pedestrian accessibility for elderly and mobility-impaired residents
Contact DOT to understand root cause (construction, weather, deferred maintenance) and timeline for repairs

themes_detail.label: Park Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Park noise complaints jumped to 10 THIS WEEK, a 1043% spike versus the 0.9-complaint weekly baseline over 8 weeks, indicating a new or intensifying disruptive activity in neighborhood parks during peak season.
evidence: 10 park noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.9 weekly average (z-score: 6.69)
1043% increase suggests new phenomenon, not gradual trend
Follows community board's repeated budget requests for park renovations and upgrades, indicating sustained underinvestment in park management
reporting_angles: Visit parks during peak complaint times; identify noise sources (music venues, events, construction, crowds) and interview residents about impact on park use
Cross-reference with NYC Parks permits and event schedules; determine if new programming or commercial activity is driving complaints

themes_detail.label: Dead/Dying Trees Spike
themes_detail.summary: Dead or dying tree complaints surged to 6 THIS WEEK, a 1100% jump from the 0.5-complaint weekly average over 8 weeks, pointing to potential pest infestation, disease outbreak, or drought stress affecting the urban forest.
evidence: 6 dead/dying tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average (z-score: 5.5)
1100% increase suggests acute environmental stressor, not normal seasonal variation
Aligns with street light condition spike (26 complaints last week), suggesting broader infrastructure and environmental decline
reporting_angles: Consult NYC Parks and arborists about potential causes (emerald ash borer, disease, heat stress, lack of watering) and whether this is part of a citywide pattern
Document specific tree locations and species; assess whether tree mortality correlates with underwatered block areas or recent construction

themes_detail.label: Asbestos Detection Cluster
themes_detail.summary: Asbestos complaints jumped to 6 THIS WEEK, a 500% increase from the 1.0-complaint weekly average over 8 weeks, raising concerns about building code enforcement and potential exposure risk during renovation season.
evidence: 6 asbestos complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.0 weekly average (z-score: 4.08)
500% spike coincides with high DOB filing activity (1,161 total, 1,081 alterations in last 90 days), suggesting renovation work may be exposing hazardous materials
Community board has repeatedly requested expanded code enforcement (Department of Buildings), indicating pre-existing enforcement gaps
reporting_angles: Identify addresses of asbestos complaints and determine if renovations were underway; assess whether DOB is conducting proper hazmat inspections before alteration work begins
Interview residents about exposure concerns and DOB response times; determine if asbestos abatement protocols are being followed in older UWS buildings

themes_detail.label: Street Light Infrastructure Decline
themes_detail.summary: Street light complaints rose to 26 LAST WEEK, a 160% increase from the 10.0-complaint weekly average over 8 weeks, indicating accelerating electrical or maintenance failures that compromise evening safety and visibility.
evidence: 26 street light complaints LAST WEEK vs. 10.0 weekly average (z-score: 5.75)
160% increase sustained over last week, suggesting systemic electrical or bulb failure rather than isolated incidents
Helicopter noise also spiked 151% last week (333 vs. 132.5 avg), indicating potential weather event or citywide infrastructure disruption last week
reporting_angles: Contact Con Edison and NYC DOT to determine cause of outages (equipment failure, power surge, scheduled maintenance); obtain timeline for repairs
Document dark blocks at night; assess whether street light failures correlate with reported crime or pedestrian safety concerns
